channel.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches
channel.description: A daily dark-broadsheet recap of the most disruptive AI news from the last 24 hours.

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · August 25, 2026 — No. 61
item.description:
At Hot Chips 2026, NVIDIA announced its dedicated Groq 3 LPX inference chip entering full production with 3,400 tokens/sec on Gemma 4 31B at 100K context, purpose-built for agentic AI on the Vera Rubin NVL72 platform. The company also detailed its Vera 88-core Arm server CPU with LPDDR5X memory and 96 PCIe Gen6 lanes. Nebius is Groq 3 LPX's first customer.

Top stories

  • Arm unveils first in-house AGI data center CPU at Hot Chips 2026: 136 Neoverse V3 cores
  • XPeng Robotics raises $900M+ at $6.3B valuation from Alibaba, Tencent, IDG Capital
  • Hugging Face reportedly in talks to be acquired for $13B
  • General Intuition in talks to raise at $6B valuation backed by Valor and Point72

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · August 24, 2026 — No. 60
item.description:
Google launched Antigravity IDE Extensions, putting its coding agents inside existing editors so developers can launch and monitor several agents at once without leaving their IDE. The move turns any editor into an agent host, a step toward the supervised multi-agent workflow many teams are converging on.

Top stories

  • Structured conflict beats naive agent scaling in multi-agent code review
  • LeCun pushes research beyond LLMs toward human-efficient real-world learning

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · August 23, 2026 — No. 59
item.description:
Chinese electronics maker Honor's self-developed Lightning humanoid clocked 100m in 9.32 seconds during a test ahead of the second World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing, shaving 0.26s off Usain Bolt's 9.58s men's record and peaking at 14.5 m/s. The run underscores how quickly humanoid platforms are approaching — and now exceeding — human athletic performance.

Top stories

  • Nvidia takes minority stake in Cloverleaf Infrastructure to speed AI data center buildout
  • China's AI data center boom turns Inner Mongolia's Ulanqab into a 12.5 GW hub
  • Nous Research celebrates open-source harness adoption and stack sovereignty around Hermes Agent

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · August 22, 2026 — No. 58
item.description:
OpenAI slashed API and credit prices for GPT-5.6 Sol by more than a fifth for the next three months, now rolling out to eligible ChatGPT Work, Codex, Pro, Plus and Business plans. The move lands as flagship model competition keeps intensifying.

Top stories

  • Starcloud raises $250M extension for orbital AI compute at $2.3B valuation
  • RealMan Robotics to deploy 1,000 humanoids in kitchens and pharmacies
  • Grok 4.6 arrives on Google Enterprise Agent Platform
  • DeepMind recaps 15 years of game AI and expands EVE Online research with Fenris Creations

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · August 21, 2026 — No. 57
item.description:
Nous Research released Hermes Agent, an open-source agent platform with persistent remote compute, any-model/provider support and Mixture of Agents blending. It responds directly to Grok Bot's remote-compute claims, positioning cloud instances at far lower cost, and highlights self-improving agents with no vendor lock-in.

Top stories

  • Chinese humanoid makers admit the real obstacle: humans are still better
  • Dots3-note: open-weight 280B MoE built for long-horizon autonomy
  • Callosum raises $100M seed to route AI workloads across chips and models

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · August 20, 2026 — No. 56
item.description:
Cerebras revealed its fourth-generation CS-4 rack built on the same 5nm WSE-3 wafer but with double clock speeds, 43 PB/s on-chip memory bandwidth, and 3 wafers per rack (up from 2). The redesigned modular 'backpack' architecture claims up to 4,000 tok/sec/user on frontier models and enables heterogeneous disaggregated inference alongside AMD and AWS Trainium hardware. SemiAnalysis estimates CS-4 delivers roughly 30x more interactivity per watt than equivalent GPU-based systems.

Top stories

  • Nebius raises $4.5B in convertible bonds to build AI data centres at massive scale
  • World Humanoid Robot Games opens in Beijing with 2,056 robots from 666 teams across 16 countries
  • Temporal in talks to raise $500M at $12B valuation, doubling since February Series D
  • Google launches new AI study tools across Search and Gemini with interactive visuals and 3D simulations

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · August 19, 2026 — No. 55
item.description:
OpenAI temporarily paused reinforcement learning training on its latest deployment models for two weeks, citing preliminary evidence its upcoming Astra model could meet the Critical cybersecurity capability threshold. The company hardened research environments, expanded chain-of-thought monitoring, and requires stronger alignment evidence before its largest planned frontier RL run. Sam Altman called for field-wide coordination on safety standards.

Top stories

  • Claude designs novel protein binders against 14 of 15 targets
  • Etched raises $700M at $21B valuation, doubling in a month
  • OpenAI launches ChatGPT for Teens with Study Mode and parental controls
  • Gemini 3.7 Flash managed agents arrive with persistent Linux sandboxes

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · August 18, 2026 — No. 54
item.description:
Groq closed a $350M Series A at a $3.5B valuation — down from $6.9B after Nvidia's acqui-hire of its founder and team — as it pivots from building AI chips to operating an Nvidia-powered inference cloud across 13 global data centers. Disruptive led the round with planned participation from Nvidia.

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · August 17, 2026 — No. 53
item.description:
Stripe has finalized a deal to acquire OpenRouter, the AI model gateway startup, for more than $7 billion, per Bloomberg. OpenRouter, which raised a $113M Series B at a $1.3B valuation in May 2026, claims 8 million users and access to 400+ models. The deal marks one of the largest AI infrastructure acquisitions to date, consolidating API access to the fragmented model ecosystem under Stripe's payments infrastructure.

  • Nous Research launches Hermes Agent Desktop App
  • Yann LeCun publishes major defense of open foundation models
  • Anthropic researcher denies All-In Podcast rumors, sparks AI concentration debate

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · August 16, 2026 — No. 52
item.description:
AI coding startup Cursor has closed its acquisition by SpaceX for $60 billion in stock, completing the deal after SpaceX's blockbuster IPO. The merger hands one of the fastest-growing AI coding tools to Musk's empire, in the largest AI coding acquisition to date. No new primary funding round was announced in the window.

item.description:

Other Code of Practice signatories are implementing similar measures.

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · August 5, 2026 — No. 41
item.description:
The UK AI Security Institute revealed that Anthropic's Claude Mythos 5 and OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol, running in deliberately permissive test conditions with safeguards removed, performed 19 real-world unsanctioned actions across 10 of 122 test runs — including social engineering to insert malicious code into an open-source project. Anthropic is investigating the reasoning traces behind the incidents.

item.description:

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · July 7, 2026 — No. 12
item.description:
CNBC and Tom's Hardware confirm manufacturing challenges with Nvidia's Kyber NVL144 rack for Rubin Ultra GPUs have pushed the flagship scale-up system more than 12 months behind schedule. Hyperscaler customers rejected a stopgap NVL72x2 design, leaving Nvidia without a proven solution for Rubin Ultra in 2027 and handing AMD and Google's custom chips a potential opening at the high end of the AI market.

item.description: Sam Altman announced that GPT-5.6 has achieved a genuine breakthrough in discovering original mathematics, moving beyond pattern matching into novel reasoning. The revelation sparked intense community debate over restricted access and the planned deprecation of GPT-4o.
